reserveReview.rationale: Retrieved on October 15, 2026, the public LedgerLens loader exposes snapshot 6acf6eec0ff131db2a33fe2c at 2026-10-14T12:00:44.764Z. Gross FBO inventory is $1,007,516.78: nine positive Treasury-bill CUSIPs total $357,140.86, two positive repo positions total $600,000 and cash is $50,375.92. The complete positive item roster, category totals and FBO account reconcile. Gross-inventory weights rounded to two decimals total 100%. The separately disclosed $39,464.93 administration payable yields $968,051.85 net reserves against $968,051.849913 exact eight-deployment liabilities; its allocation across reserve categories remains unknown. Current pinned native supplies independently sum to that liability figure, but are not substituted for canonical circulating USD supply. The positive bill roster now includes December 1, 2026 maturity 912797VZ7 and excludes the zero-balance matured 912797VL8; the latest observed maturity is 48 calendar days after the snapshot, not a contractual maximum. The two positive repos mature on the snapshot date; neither that record nor an overnight label proves stressed cash availability. Current reserve rules, effective September 23, 2026, Chapter 3 section 4(b), limit Treasury securities to 365 days and Treasury repos to 30 days and also permit Rule 2a-7 money-market funds; no MMF position is observed. The issuer website's narrower overnight-only eligibility wording is not substituted for the governing rule. The dashboard expressly excludes its metrics from TNF's separately issued AT-C 205 opinions and says it is not FRNT's accounting or internal-control system. Verified denotes source-inventory and arithmetic verification, not independent financial assurance. No signed report opinion, contractual cash maturity, repo or cash counterparty allocation, subcustody, reuse protection, or whole-position stressed settlement guarantee is inferred. The statutory liquidity-fund target is not asserted as measured 102% coverage.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Non-assured gross FBO fair-market-value inventory; net reserves separately deduct due-to-administration
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Asset classes are itemized; repo and cash-account counterparties and the allocation of the administration payable across assets are not. FTI and BNY Mellon are disclosed custodial layers, without account agreements or allocated shares. The October 14 dashboard reports a zero liquidity-fund balance; the law creates a separate 2% liquidity account and prioritizes funding after operating costs, leaving its current funding and dashboard scope to be reconciled. Supplemental metrics establish neither financial assurance nor statutory noncompliance.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: The Commission identifies Fiduciary Trust International as reserve custodian and Franklin Advisers as portfolio manager; LedgerLens identifies Bank of New York Mellon as subcustodian. No allocation shares are disclosed. Chapter 3 requires holder-benefit trust accounts separate from liquidity and administration accounts; Chapter 2 limits the special obligation to trust assets. The rules also say opening or funding the accounts does not create a Commission fiduciary duty to holders. Actual trust/subcustody agreements, cash and repo counterparty allocation, enforceable reuse restrictions and custody replacement mechanics were not retrieved, so whole-book institutional custody and verified bankruptcy remoteness remain unestablished. The claim carries no state full-faith-and-credit or federal deposit-insurance guarantee.
